codeReview.summary: The fix addresses the original quoted-argument fragmentation from `str.split()`, but it introduces a new blocking regression for existing regex scenarios that rely on backslash escapes, so the original failure is not adequately resolved.

issues.description: Using `shlex.split(cmd_str)` strips unquoted backslashes from existing regex patterns (e.g. `\b...\b`), changing argv semantics for existing non-space scenarios. Evidence from the reviewed commits: original scenario `regex-complex` uses unquoted `{pattern}` (`manifests/scenarios.json:93` in commit `45832a8...`) with query pattern `\b[A-Z]{2,}_[A-Z]{2,}\b` (`manifests/queries.json:52` in commit `45832a8...`), while fix commit tokenization turns that argument into `b[A-Z]{2,}_[A-Z]{2,}b`.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Shared guidance does not document command-template escaping rules for scenario manifests (quoted vs unquoted `{pattern}`), which made this argv-tokenization fix regress existing escaped-regex behavior.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: AGENTS.md and .factory/library docs emphasize parity/reproducibility but do not specify manifest command escaping conventions; manifests/scenarios.json (commit 45832a8..., line 93) uses unquoted `{pattern}` while manifests/queries.json (line 52) contains escaped regex boundaries.

sharedStateObservations.observation: `rewrite-worker` remains Rust-centric and does not explicitly force Python tooling edge-case coverage for argv parsing, despite this mission containing Python parity tooling where shell-tokenization semantics are subtle.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: .factory/skills/rewrite-worker/SKILL.md step 4 says 'Implement Rust changes', while this feature changed Python (`scripts/parity/run_matrix.py`) and transcript skeleton for session f0c71383-e61e-45c6-8477-b732e09e10fa focused on Python/manifests.

summary: Reviewed fix feature `baseline-parity-argv-tokenization-fix`, its transcript skeleton, prior failed review, and both relevant diffs (`45832a8...` and `fec364e...`).
